options.method: POST https://www.pcbway.com/Quote/GetDeliveryDays/ (anonymous; partVias=1 turnkey, hidAssemblySide=3 top side). Recipe: /tmp/pcbway-quote-recipe.md

notes: PCB cost: via in pad on a 4/4mil board is the main cost driver. It adds $463.65 and moves the build from 4-5 days to 8-9 days, the only build option. The fab notes ask for 0.11 mm track/clearance, which needs PCBWay's 4/4mil class; the same options at 5/5mil would be $196.33. Via in pad: the fab notes require IPC-4761 Type VII fill and capping only at the 18 sites in via-in-pad.csv and allow ordinary vias to be tented. Fab notes give 35 um finished copper on all four layers, quoted as 1 oz outer and 1 oz inner. 100% e-test has no form field; PCBWay flying-probe tests every PCB. Assembly, top side only (no bottom parts): normal price = max($88, $25.27 + $0.1523 x 93 parts x qty), so $88 for 1 board and $96.10 for 5. $29 promo: one board qualifies (93 parts, 55 unique, 24 THT joints from J5 2x10 and J6 1x4). Five boards do not, because 24 x 5 = 120 THT joints exceeds the 100-joint order limit; the instant quote can't check joints and still shows $29. Struck-through 'list' prices next to $29: $299.73 (qty 1) and $306.32 (qty 5), from the qty >= 11 formula, not charged here. The form has no IPC-4761 Type VII choice or 90 ohm target field; those go in the order notes and are confirmed at file review.
